title: Technology & Learning - Professional Learning
before:
Maple Bytes Professional Learning Modules

Maple Bytes is a Maine Department of Education–developed interdisciplinary instructional program that invites students to explore the science and cultural significance of maple syrup through a unique blend of Wabanaki Studies, Computer Science, and Earth Science. Designed by Maine DOE’s specialists Allison Braley, Erik Wade, and Brianne Lolar, this lesson provides a rich, place-based learning experience grounded in both traditional knowledge and modern technology.

Learn More

AI Guidance Toolkit for Schools and Educators

This dynamic resource goes beyond traditional policies, pairing guidance with learning by offering practical tools, real-world scenarios, and ongoing learning opportunities that support ethical, responsible, and effective AI use. Grounded in digital citizenship and computer science foundations, this toolkit is designed to enhance the understanding and application of artificial intelligence in education.

decisions.label: Tag a document link with the format it opens
decisions.why: 2 links on this page open a file — 2 Video — and say nothing about it, while others in the same list carry a tag because their author typed one. The format is read from the file name, so the list stops being half-labelled. No link text changes.

decisions.label: Put the card titles on one level
decisions.why: 2 card titles are written at a level copied from an example rather than chosen — h5 on a page whose sections are h2. Only the number changes.

decisions.label: Put the buttons on the house style
decisions.why: 2 buttons use a Bootstrap variant rather than btn-info, so the same kind of action is drawn three different ways across the site. Only the class changes.

decisions.label: Make a loose address look like an address
decisions.why: 1 email address sits in the body of this page rather than in a contact block, drawn exactly like every other link — so the one that opens a mail window looks the same as the ones that go to web pages. The chip carries the same envelope the banner's contact link uses. The address itself does not change.

decisions.label: Retire the old banner graphic
decisions.why: It repeats the page title in picture form, which the new banner already does in type.
